questions.prompt: Class A has 20 students with a mean test score of 78. Class B has 30 students with a mean test score of 88. What is the mean test score of all 50 students?
questions.explanation: The total of all scores is 20(78) + 30(88) = 1,560 + 2,640 = 4,200, and 4,200 / 50 = 84. Averaging the two class means to get 83 ignores that Class B has more students.

questions.prompt: The table shows values of x and y. Which equation best models the relationship between x and y?
questions.explanation: Each time x increases by 1, y doubles, which indicates exponential growth with initial value 3 and growth factor 2. The linear model y = 3x + 3 matches the first two pairs but gives 9, not 12, when x = 2.

questions.prompt: A line of best fit for a data set is y = 1.2x + 5.3. One data point in the set is (10, 19.8). What is the residual for this data point (actual y-value minus predicted y-value)?
questions.explanation: The predicted value is 1.2(10) + 5.3 = 17.3, so the residual is 19.8 - 17.3 = 2.5. Subtracting in the other order gives -2.5, which is predicted minus actual.

questions.prompt: A line of best fit for a scatterplot passes through the points (2, 14) and (8, 32). What y-value does this line predict when x = 15?
questions.explanation: The slope is (32 - 14)/(8 - 2) = 3, so the line is y = 3x + 8. When x = 15, y = 3(15) + 8 = 53.

questions.prompt: The value, in dollars, of a car t years after it was purchased is modeled by V = 24,000(0.85)^t. Which statement best interprets the number 0.85 in this model?
options: The car's value decreases by 85% each year.
The car's value decreases by $0.85 each year.
The car's value increases by 85% each year.
The car's value decreases by 15% each year.
questions.explanation: Multiplying by 0.85 each year keeps 85% of the value, which means the value decreases by 100% - 85% = 15% per year. A decrease of 85% would correspond to a factor of 0.15, not 0.85.

questions.prompt: The table shows 6 data points. Which of the following is closest to the slope of the line of best fit for these data?
questions.explanation: As x increases by 1, y increases by roughly 2 each time (for example, from 3.1 to 4.9 to 7.2), so the slope is closest to 2. The value 0.5 is the reciprocal of the slope, which describes the change in x per unit change in y.

table.caption: Preferred hot drink by age group

questions.prompt: The table shows the results of a survey of 200 people about their preferred hot drink. If a person who prefers tea is selected at random, what is the probability that the person is under 30 years old?
questions.explanation: The condition limits the group to the 85 people who prefer tea, and 35 of them are under 30, so the probability is 35/85 = 7/17. The fraction 7/16 equals 35/80, which instead finds the probability of preferring tea given being under 30.

questions.prompt: Two fair coins are tossed. What is the probability that at least one coin lands heads up?
questions.explanation: The four equally likely outcomes are HH, HT, TH, and TT, and three of them contain at least one head, so the probability is 3/4. The answer 2/3 incorrectly treats 'two heads', 'one head', and 'no heads' as equally likely.

questions.prompt: A jar contains 4 red marbles and 6 blue marbles. Two marbles are drawn at random without replacement. What is the probability that both marbles are red?
questions.explanation: The probability that the first marble is red is 4/10, and then 3 of the remaining 9 marbles are red, so the probability is (4/10)(3/9) = 12/90 = 2/15. Using (4/10)(4/10) = 4/25 would treat the draws as being made with replacement.

questions.prompt: The table shows the number of juniors and seniors at a school who do or do not play a sport. If a student who plays a sport is selected at random, what is the probability that the student is a senior?
questions.explanation: Among the 114 students who play a sport, 66 are seniors, so the probability is 66/114 = 11/19. The fraction 11/20 equals 66/120, which is the probability that a senior plays a sport, the reverse condition.

questions.prompt: The probability that a certain machine part is defective is 0.035. Based on this probability, how many defective parts are expected in a batch of 4,000 parts?
questions.explanation: The expected number of defective parts is 0.035 x 4,000 = 140. The value 3,860 is the expected number of parts that are not defective.

questions.skill: Inference from sample statistics and margin of error
questions.prompt: A random sample of students at a university found a mean of 24.5 hours per week spent studying, with a margin of error of 1.8 hours at a 95% confidence level. Which conclusion is most appropriate?
options: Every student at the university studies between 22.7 and 26.3 hours per week.
The mean study time for all students at the university is exactly 24.5 hours per week.
The mean study time for all students at the university cannot be greater than 24.5 hours per week.
It is plausible that the mean study time for all students at the university is between 22.7 and 26.3 hours per week.
questions.explanation: A margin of error describes plausible values for the population mean: 24.5 - 1.8 = 22.7 to 24.5 + 1.8 = 26.3. It does not describe the range of individual students' values, and the sample mean is only an estimate, not the exact population mean.

questions.skill: Inference from sample statistics and margin of error
questions.prompt: Two researchers each select a random sample from the same population of adults to estimate the mean number of hours of sleep per night. Researcher 1 uses a sample of 400 adults, and Researcher 2 uses a sample of 100 adults. Both use the same confidence level. Which statement is most likely true?
options: Researcher 2's estimate will have a smaller margin of error.
Both estimates will have the same margin of error.
Researcher 1's estimate will have a smaller margin of error.
Researcher 1's estimate will be exactly equal to the population mean.
questions.explanation: With all else equal, a larger random sample produces a smaller margin of error, so the sample of 400 should give a more precise estimate. A larger sample does not guarantee that the estimate exactly equals the population mean.

questions.skill: Inference from sample statistics and margin of error
questions.prompt: A store randomly selected 80 of the 2,400 lightbulbs it received and found that 6 of the selected bulbs were defective. Based on this sample, what is the best estimate of the number of defective lightbulbs among the 2,400 bulbs?
questions.explanation: The sample proportion is 6/80 = 0.075, and 0.075 x 2,400 = 180. This estimate is reasonable because the sample was selected at random from the shipment.

questions.skill: Inference from sample statistics and margin of error
questions.prompt: A poll of a random sample of likely voters found that 52% support a ballot measure, with a margin of error of 3.5 percentage points. Which conclusion is best supported by the poll?
options: The measure will definitely pass because 52% is more than half.
Exactly 52% of all likely voters support the measure.
It is not clear whether more than half of all likely voters support the measure.
Fewer than half of all likely voters support the measure.
questions.explanation: The plausible values are 52 - 3.5 = 48.5% to 52 + 3.5 = 55.5%, an interval that includes values both below and above 50%. Therefore the poll does not establish that a majority supports the measure, and it does not establish that a minority does either.

questions.skill: Inference from sample statistics and margin of error
questions.prompt: In a random sample of 200 adults from a city of 90,000 adults, 38% said they use public transit. The margin of error for this estimate is 4 percentage points. Based on this information, which range contains plausible values for the number of adults in the city who use public transit?
questions.explanation: Plausible percents are 38 - 4 = 34% to 38 + 4 = 42%, and 0.34 x 90,000 = 30,600 while 0.42 x 90,000 = 37,800. The range 34,200 to 37,800 starts at the point estimate, 0.38 x 90,000, instead of subtracting the margin of error.

questions.skill: Evaluating statistical claims: observational studies and experiments
questions.prompt: Researchers selected a random sample of 500 adults from a large city. Each adult reported the number of cups of coffee they drink per day and the number of hours they sleep per night. The researchers found that adults who drank more coffee tended to sleep fewer hours. Which conclusion is best supported?
options: Drinking more coffee causes adults in the city to sleep less.
Drinking more coffee causes all adults to sleep less.
The association applies only to the 500 adults in the sample and cannot be generalized to the city.
Among adults in the city, coffee consumption is associated with less sleep, but it cannot be concluded that coffee causes less sleep.
questions.explanation: Because the sample was randomly selected from the city, the association can be generalized to the city's adults. Because no treatment was randomly assigned, the study cannot show that coffee causes less sleep.

questions.skill: Evaluating statistical claims: observational studies and experiments
questions.prompt: A company recruited 300 volunteers and randomly assigned half of them to use a new memory-training app daily and the other half to play an unrelated game daily. After 8 weeks, the app group scored significantly higher on a memory test. Which statement is best supported?
options: The app likely causes improved memory scores for people similar to the volunteers.
The app likely causes improved memory scores for all people.
The study shows only an association, so no causal conclusion is possible.
The app does not improve memory, because the participants were volunteers.
questions.explanation: Random assignment allows a causal conclusion, but because the volunteers were not randomly selected from a larger population, the conclusion applies only to people like the volunteers. Calling the result only an association ignores the role of random assignment.

questions.skill: Evaluating statistical claims: observational studies and experiments
questions.prompt: A study found that students who eat breakfast every day have higher average grades than students who do not. Which of the following, if true, gives the best reason to doubt that eating breakfast causes higher grades?
options: The study included students from several grade levels.
Some students who eat breakfast have low grades.
The study measured grades at the end of the school year.
Students who eat breakfast every day also tend to get more sleep each night.
questions.explanation: If breakfast eaters also sleep more, sleep is a possible confounding variable that could explain the higher grades. A few breakfast eaters with low grades does not contradict an association based on averages.

questions.skill: Evaluating statistical claims: observational studies and experiments
questions.prompt: A teacher wants to compare two methods of teaching fractions. She teaches her morning class with Method 1 and her afternoon class with Method 2, then compares test scores. Which change to the study would best support a conclusion that one method causes higher scores?
options: Give the test to the classes a second time.
Compare only the students with the highest scores in each class.
Randomly assign the students to the two methods instead of using the existing classes.
questions.explanation: Morning and afternoon classes may differ in ways that affect scores, so differences could be due to the class rather than the method. Randomly assigning students to methods balances these differences, which supports a cause-and-effect conclusion.

questions.skill: Ratios, rates, proportional relationships, and units
questions.prompt: A car averages 32 miles per gallon of gasoline, and gasoline costs $3.60 per gallon. A trip is 440 kilometers long. If 1 mile is 1.6 kilometers, which of the following is closest to the cost of the gasoline needed for the trip?
questions.explanation: The trip is 440 / 1.6 = 275 miles, which requires 275 / 32 = 8.59375 gallons, costing 8.59375 x 3.60 = about $30.94. The value $49.50 treats 440 kilometers as 440 miles, skipping the unit conversion.

questions.skill: Ratios, rates, proportional relationships, and units
questions.prompt: Pipe A alone can fill a tank in 6 hours, and Pipe B alone can fill the same tank in 9 hours. If both pipes are opened at the same time, how many hours will it take to fill the empty tank?
questions.explanation: Pipe A fills 1/6 of the tank per hour and Pipe B fills 1/9, so together they fill 1/6 + 1/9 = 5/18 of the tank per hour. The time is 18/5 = 3.6 hours; averaging the times (7.5 hours) is a common error, since working together must be faster than either pipe alone.

questions.skill: Ratios, rates, proportional relationships, and units
questions.prompt: A solid cube with an edge length of 4 centimeters has a mass of 1.6 kilograms. What is the density of the cube, in grams per cubic centimeter? (1 kilogram = 1,000 grams)
questions.explanation: The volume is 4^3 = 64 cubic centimeters and the mass is 1,600 grams, so the density is 1,600 / 64 = 25 grams per cubic centimeter. Using 4^2 = 16 as the volume gives 100, which uses area instead of volume.

questions.skill: Ratios, rates, proportional relationships, and units
questions.prompt: The ratio of a to b is 2 to 3, and the ratio of b to c is 4 to 5. What is the ratio of a to c?
questions.explanation: Multiply the ratios: a/c = (a/b)(b/c) = (2/3)(4/5) = 8/15. Combining the first term of one ratio with the last term of the other, as in 2 to 5, ignores that b must be scaled to the same value in both ratios.

questions.skill: Ratios, rates, proportional relationships, and units
questions.prompt: A rectangular garden measuring 18 feet by 24 feet will be covered with a layer of mulch 3 inches deep. Mulch is sold in bags that each contain 2 cubic feet. What is the minimum number of bags needed? (12 inches = 1 foot)
questions.explanation: The depth is 3/12 = 0.25 foot, so the volume is 18 x 24 x 0.25 = 108 cubic feet, which requires 108 / 2 = 54 bags. Using 3 feet as the depth would overstate the volume by a factor of 12.

questions.skill: Ratios, rates, proportional relationships, and units
questions.prompt: The quantity y is directly proportional to the square of x. When x = 4, y = 48. What is the value of y when x = 6?
questions.explanation: Write y = kx^2; then 48 = k(16), so k = 3 and y = 3(36) = 108 when x = 6. The value 72 results from treating y as proportional to x instead of x^2.

questions.prompt: A store marks up the cost of an item by 40% to set its regular price. During a sale, the store sells the item at 25% off the regular price. The sale price is what percent of the original cost?
questions.explanation: The sale price is (1.40)(0.75) = 1.05 times the cost, which is 105% of the cost. Subtracting the percents (40% - 25% = 15%) to get 115% ignores that the discount applies to the larger, marked-up price.

questions.prompt: The price of a stock increased by p% on Monday and then decreased by p% on Tuesday. At the end of Tuesday, the price was 9% less than it was at the start of Monday. What is the value of p?
The population of Town A is 25% greater than the population of Town B. The population of Town B is what percent less than the population of Town A?
questions.explanation: If B = 100, then A = 125, and B is 25 less than A; 25/125 = 0.20, so B is 20% less than A. Answering 25% uses B instead of A as the base.

questions.prompt: A chemist has 40 liters of a solution that is 15% acid. How many liters of pure acid must be added to produce a solution that is 25% acid?
questions.explanation: The solution contains 0.15(40) = 6 liters of acid, so (6 + x)/(40 + x) = 0.25, which gives 6 + x = 10 + 0.25x, and x = 4/0.75 = 16/3. Answering 4 adds acid without increasing the total volume of the solution.

questions.prompt: A quantity increases by 10% each year for 3 years. By what percent does the quantity increase over the entire 3-year period?
questions.explanation: The quantity is multiplied by 1.1^3 = 1.331, which is a 33.1% increase. Adding 10% three times to get 30% ignores that each increase applies to a larger amount.

questions.prompt: A company's sales in 2020 were 20% greater than its sales in 2019. Its sales in 2021 were 15% less than its sales in 2020. If the company sold 5,100 units in 2021, how many units did it sell in 2019?
questions.explanation: Sales in 2021 equal the 2019 sales times (1.20)(0.85) = 1.02, so 2019 sales = 5,100 / 1.02 = 5,000. Reversing the percents by adding 15% and subtracting 20% from 5,100 uses the wrong bases.

questions.skill: One-variable data: distributions and measures of center and spread
questions.prompt: A data set has mean m and standard deviation s, where s > 0. Each value in the data set is multiplied by 3, and then 4 is added to each result. What are the mean and standard deviation of the new data set?
questions.explanation: Multiplying every value by 3 multiplies both the mean and the spread by 3, and adding 4 shifts the mean by 4 but does not change the spread. So the new mean is 3m + 4 and the new standard deviation is 3s; adding 4 to the standard deviation is the most common error.

questions.skill: One-variable data: distributions and measures of center and spread
questions.prompt: The frequency table shows the distribution of a data set, where k is a positive integer. The mean of the data set is 2.6. What is the value of k?
questions.explanation: The sum of the values is 4(1) + 2k + 6(3) + 5(4) = 42 + 2k, and the number of values is 15 + k. Solving (42 + 2k)/(15 + k) = 2.6 gives 42 + 2k = 39 + 2.6k, so k = 5.

questions.skill: One-variable data: distributions and measures of center and spread
questions.prompt: The frequency table shows the number of siblings for each of 50 students. Which statement correctly compares the mean and the median of the data?
options: The median is greater than the mean by 0.4.
The mean is greater than the median by 0.5.
The mean and the median are equal.
The mean is greater than the median by 0.4.
questions.explanation: The total number of siblings is 0 + 20 + 18 + 15 + 12 + 5 = 70, so the mean is 70/50 = 1.4. The 25th and 26th values both fall in the group with 1 sibling (positions 13 through 32), so the median is 1 and the mean is greater by 0.4.

questions.skill: One-variable data: distributions and measures of center and spread
questions.prompt: A data set contains 9 different values. A tenth value, equal to the mean of the original 9 values, is added to the data set. Which statement about the new data set is true?
options: The mean is unchanged, and the standard deviation decreases.
The mean is unchanged, and the standard deviation is unchanged.
The mean is unchanged, and the standard deviation increases.
The mean increases, and the standard deviation decreases.
questions.explanation: Adding a value equal to the mean keeps the sum of deviations at zero, so the mean does not change. The new value has a deviation of 0, so the same total squared deviation is spread over more values, and the standard deviation decreases; it does not stay the same.

questions.skill: One-variable data: distributions and measures of center and spread
questions.prompt: A data set of 7 integers has a mean of 10, a median of 9, a range of 12, and a unique mode of 8. What is the greatest possible value in the data set?
questions.explanation: Order the values a1 through a7 with a4 = 9, sum 70, and a7 = a1 + 12; the mode 8 needs at least two 8s, which must come before the median. If a1 = 8 or a1 = 7, the remaining values cannot reach a sum of 70 without repeating a value as often as 8 or breaking the order, but a1 = 6 works with 6, 8, 8, 9, 10, 11, 18. So the greatest possible value is 18; 20 fails because it would require a1 = 8.

questions.skill: One-variable data: distributions and measures of center and spread
questions.prompt: The mean of a data set of n values is 40. When a new value of 85 is added to the data set, the mean becomes 43. What is the value of n?
questions.explanation: The original sum is 40n and the new sum is 40n + 85 = 43(n + 1). Then 40n + 85 = 43n + 43, so 3n = 42 and n = 14.

questions.prompt: An exponential model of the form y = a(b)^x, where a and b are positive constants, passes through the points (1, 12) and (3, 108). What value of y does the model predict when x = 4?
questions.explanation: Dividing 108 = ab^3 by 12 = ab gives b^2 = 9, so b = 3 and a = 4. Then y = 4(3)^4 = 324; the value 156 comes from extending the points as if they were linear.

questions.prompt: The table shows five pairs of values of x and y. Which equation could represent the relationship between x and y?
questions.explanation: The y-values are symmetric about x = 0 with a minimum of -3, which suggests a quadratic with vertex (0, -3). Checking x = 1 gives 2(1) - 3 = -1 and x = 2 gives 2(4) - 3 = 5, while y = x^2 - 3 gives -2 at x = 1, which does not match.

questions.prompt: A line of best fit for data about a company's monthly advertising spending x, in thousands of dollars, and its monthly sales y, in thousands of dollars, is y = 0.45x + 12.6. According to the model, if advertising spending increases by $8,000, by how many dollars are monthly sales predicted to increase?
questions.explanation: An increase of $8,000 means x increases by 8, so y increases by 0.45 x 8 = 3.6 thousand dollars, or $3,600. Substituting x = 8 into the full equation gives 16.2 thousand, which is a predicted sales level, not a change.

questions.prompt: A linear model for a set of data has a slope of -2.4 and predicts y = 30 when x = 5. One data point in the set is (12, 9.8). What is the residual for this data point (actual y-value minus predicted y-value)?
questions.explanation: The model predicts y = 30 - 2.4(12 - 5) = 30 - 16.8 = 13.2 at x = 12. The residual is 9.8 - 13.2 = -3.4, which is negative because the data point lies below the line.

questions.prompt: In a certain town, 60% of residents are adults and 40% are children. Of the adults, 30% have a library card, and of the children, 70% have a library card. If a resident with a library card is selected at random, what is the probability that the resident is an adult?
questions.explanation: Adults with cards make up 0.6(0.3) = 0.18 of residents and children with cards make up 0.4(0.7) = 0.28, so 0.46 of residents have cards. The probability is 0.18/0.46 = 9/23; the value 3/10 is the probability that an adult has a card, which reverses the condition.

table.caption: Club members by age and driving status

questions.prompt: The table shows the members of a club classified by age and by whether they drive. If a member who drives is selected at random, the probability that the member is 18 or older is 0.75. What is the value of x?
questions.explanation: Among drivers, the probability of being 18 or older is x/(12 + x) = 0.75. Then x = 0.75(12 + x) = 9 + 0.75x, so 0.25x = 9 and x = 36.

questions.prompt: A box contains 20 batteries, 5 of which are defective. If 3 batteries are selected at random without replacement, what is the probability that at least one of the selected batteries is defective?
questions.explanation: The probability that none is defective is C(15, 3)/C(20, 3) = 455/1140 = 91/228, so the probability of at least one defective battery is 1 - 91/228 = 137/228. The value 37/64 = 1 - (3/4)^3 treats the selections as independent, which is only true with replacement.

questions.prompt: In a clinical trial, patients received either a treatment or a placebo. The table shows the results. If a patient who did not improve is selected at random, what is the probability that the patient received the treatment?
questions.explanation: There are 36 + 66 = 102 patients who did not improve, and 36 of them received the treatment, so the probability is 36/102 = 6/17. The value 3/10 equals 36/120, which is the probability of not improving given treatment, the reverse condition.

questions.skill: Inference from sample statistics and margin of error
questions.prompt: A random sample of 150 adults from a population was used to estimate the mean number of hours per day spent on a phone, with a margin of error of 0.4 hour. A second random sample of 600 adults is taken from the same population, and the standard deviations of the two samples are about equal. Using the same confidence level, which of the following is closest to the expected margin of error for the second sample?
questions.explanation: Margin of error is proportional to 1 divided by the square root of the sample size. The sample size is 4 times as large, so the margin of error is divided by the square root of 4, which is 2, giving about 0.2 hour; dividing by 4 to get 0.1 is a common mistake.

questions.skill: Inference from sample statistics and margin of error
questions.prompt: Two random samples were taken to estimate the percent of residents who support a policy in two different cities. In City X, the estimate was 34% with a margin of error of 4 percentage points. In City Y, the estimate was 39% with a margin of error of 4 percentage points. Which conclusion is most appropriate?
options: The percent of supporters in City Y is greater than in City X.
The data do not provide convincing evidence that the percent of supporters differs between the two cities.
The percent of supporters in City Y is exactly 5 percentage points greater than in City X.
The percent of supporters in City X is greater than in City Y.
questions.explanation: The plausible values are 30% to 38% for City X and 35% to 43% for City Y, and these intervals overlap. Because a value such as 36% is plausible for both cities, the samples do not show convincingly that the cities differ.

questions.skill: Inference from sample statistics and margin of error
questions.prompt: A random sample of 250 of the 12,000 households in a town found that 18% of the sampled households have a swimming pool. The margin of error for this estimate is 4 percentage points. Based on this information, what is the greatest plausible number of households in the town that have a swimming pool?
questions.explanation: The greatest plausible percent is 18% + 4% = 22%, and 0.22 x 12,000 = 2,640 households. Applying the percent to the sample size of 250 instead of the 12,000 households in the town is a common error.

questions.skill: Evaluating statistical claims: observational studies and experiments
questions.prompt: Researchers selected a random sample of 400 adults from a state. They then randomly assigned 200 of them to take a vitamin supplement daily and the other 200 to take a placebo daily. After one year, the supplement group had significantly fewer sick days. Which conclusion is most appropriate?
options: The supplement is associated with fewer sick days, but cause and effect cannot be concluded.
The supplement likely causes fewer sick days for adults in the state.
The supplement likely causes fewer sick days, but only for the 400 adults in the study.
The supplement likely causes fewer sick days for all adults in the country.
questions.explanation: Random selection from the state allows the results to be generalized to the state's adults, and random assignment allows a causal conclusion. The results cannot be extended to the whole country, because the sample came from only one state.

questions.skill: Evaluating statistical claims: observational studies and experiments
questions.prompt: A researcher randomly selected 300 people aged 65 and older from a national registry and randomly assigned them to either a daily walking program or no program. After 6 months, the walking group had significantly better balance scores. Which statement is NOT justified by the study?
options: A daily walking program likely improves balance for people aged 65 and older in the country.
The study's random assignment helps rule out confounding variables.
The results can be generalized to the population from which the sample was selected.
A daily walking program likely improves balance for adults of all ages in the country.
questions.explanation: The sample came only from people aged 65 and older, so the conclusion cannot be extended to adults of all ages. The other statements are justified because the participants were randomly selected from the national registry of older adults and randomly assigned to groups.

questions.skill: Evaluating statistical claims: observational studies and experiments
questions.prompt: Last year, reported bicycle thefts in a small town increased from 40 to 50, and in a nearby city they increased from 2,000 to 2,300. A news article claims, "Bicycle theft is growing faster in the town than in the city." Which statement about the claim is accurate?
options: The claim is supported because the town had a greater increase in the number of thefts.
The claim is not supported because the city had a greater percent increase.
The claim is supported by the percent increases, but the city had a greater increase in the number of thefts.
The claim cannot be evaluated because the populations are different sizes.
questions.explanation: The town's thefts rose by 10/40 = 25% while the city's rose by 300/2,000 = 15%, so the town's percent increase is greater. However, the city's increase of 300 thefts is larger than the town's increase of 10, so the claim is only supported in relative terms. (Checked: 25% > 15% and 300 > 10.)

questions.skill: Evaluating statistical claims: observational studies and experiments
questions.prompt: To estimate the average number of books read per year by adults in a city, a researcher surveyed 500 randomly selected adults who visited the city's public libraries during one month. How is the estimate from this survey most likely to compare with the true average for all adults in the city?
options: It is likely to be less than the true average, because library visitors borrow books instead of buying them.
It is likely to be accurate, because the 500 adults were randomly selected.
It is likely to be accurate, because 500 is a large sample size.
It is likely to be greater than the true average, because library visitors probably read more than typical adults.
questions.explanation: The random selection was made only from library visitors, who are likely to read more than adults in general, so the sample is biased upward. Random selection from a nonrepresentative group and a large sample size do not remove this bias.

questions.prompt: A rectangle has a length of 12 inches and a width of 7.5 inches. What is the area of the rectangle, in square inches?
questions.explanation: The area of a rectangle is length times width: 12 x 7.5 = 90 square inches. Adding the dimensions and doubling (39) gives the perimeter, not the area.

questions.prompt: A triangle has a base of 10 centimeters and a height of 6 centimeters. What is the area of the triangle, in square centimeters?
questions.explanation: The area of a triangle is one-half times base times height: (1/2)(10)(6) = 30. The value 60 forgets the factor of one-half.

questions.prompt: A rectangular box has a length of 4 feet, a width of 5 feet, and a height of 6 feet. What is the volume of the box, in cubic feet?
questions.explanation: The volume of a rectangular prism is length times width times height: 4 x 5 x 6 = 120 cubic feet. The value 148 is the surface area of the box, not its volume.

questions.prompt: A right circular cylinder has a radius of 3 meters and a height of 10 meters. What is the volume of the cylinder, in cubic meters?
questions.explanation: The volume of a cylinder is pi r^2 h = pi(3^2)(10) = 90 pi cubic meters. Using the diameter-based expression pi(2)(3)(10) = 60 pi confuses volume with lateral area.

questions.prompt: A square has a perimeter of 36 units. What is the area of the square, in square units?
questions.explanation: Each side has length 36/4 = 9, so the area is 9^2 = 81 square units. Squaring the perimeter (324) skips finding the side length first.

questions.prompt: A right triangle has legs of length 9 and 12. What is the area of the triangle?
questions.explanation: In a right triangle the legs serve as base and height, so the area is (1/2)(9)(12) = 54. The hypotenuse, 15, is not needed.

questions.prompt: A cube has a volume of 64 cubic inches. What is the length of one edge of the cube, in inches?
questions.explanation: The edge length is the cube root of the volume: 4^3 = 64, so each edge is 4 inches. The value 8 is the square root of 64, which would apply to the area of a square.

questions.prompt: A trapezoid has parallel sides of length 8 and 14 and a height of 5. What is the area of the trapezoid?
questions.explanation: The area of a trapezoid is (1/2)(b1 + b2)h = (1/2)(8 + 14)(5) = 55. Leaving out the factor of one-half gives 110.

questions.prompt: A sphere has a radius of 3 centimeters. What is the volume of the sphere, in cubic centimeters?
questions.explanation: The volume of a sphere is (4/3) pi r^3 = (4/3) pi (27) = 36 pi. The value 108 pi uses 4 pi r^3 without dividing by 3.

questions.prompt: Two angles are supplementary. One of the angles measures 48 degrees. What is the measure, in degrees, of the other angle?
questions.explanation: Supplementary angles add to 180 degrees, so the other angle is 180 - 48 = 132 degrees. The value 42 would be correct for complementary angles, which add to 90 degrees.

questions.prompt: Two angles of a triangle measure 35 degrees and 75 degrees. What is the measure, in degrees, of the third angle?
questions.explanation: The angles of a triangle add to 180 degrees, so the third angle is 180 - 35 - 75 = 70 degrees.

questions.prompt: Two lines intersect at a point. One of the angles formed measures (3x + 10) degrees, and the angle vertical to it measures (5x - 30) degrees. What is the value of x?
questions.explanation: Vertical angles are congruent, so 3x + 10 = 5x - 30, which gives 2x = 40 and x = 20. Setting the angles' sum equal to 180, as for a linear pair, gives x = 25.

questions.prompt: Parallel lines l and m are intersected by a transversal. Two same-side interior angles are formed between the parallel lines on the same side of the transversal. One of these angles measures 65 degrees. What is the measure, in degrees, of the other angle?
questions.explanation: When parallel lines are cut by a transversal, same-side interior angles are supplementary, so the other angle is 180 - 65 = 115 degrees. Alternate interior angles would be congruent at 65 degrees, but these angles are on the same side.

questions.prompt: In isosceles triangle ABC, AB = AC and angle A measures 50 degrees. What is the measure, in degrees, of angle B?
questions.explanation: Because AB = AC, the base angles B and C are congruent, so each measures (180 - 50)/2 = 65 degrees. Treating angle A as a base angle would wrongly give B = 50 degrees.

questions.prompt: In triangle PQR, angle P measures 40 degrees and angle Q measures 75 degrees. Side PR is extended beyond R to point S. What is the measure, in degrees, of angle QRS?
questions.explanation: Angle QRS is an exterior angle at R, which equals the sum of the two remote interior angles: 40 + 75 = 115 degrees. The value 65 is the interior angle at R.

questions.prompt: Two sides of a triangle have lengths 5 and 9. Which of the following could be the length of the third side?
questions.explanation: By the triangle inequality, the third side must be greater than 9 - 5 = 4 and less than 9 + 5 = 14. Only 6 is in this range; a side of 4 or 14 would make the three points lie on a straight line.

questions.prompt: Triangle ABC is similar to triangle DEF, with A corresponding to D, B to E, and C to F. If AB = 6, DE = 9, and BC = 8, what is the length of EF?
questions.explanation: The scale factor from triangle ABC to triangle DEF is 9/6 = 1.5, so EF = 1.5 x 8 = 12. Adding 3 to 8 to get 11 treats similarity as additive instead of multiplicative.

questions.prompt: What is the sum of the measures, in degrees, of the interior angles of a hexagon?
questions.explanation: The interior angles of an n-sided polygon sum to (n - 2)180 degrees, so a hexagon's angles sum to 4(180) = 720 degrees.

questions.prompt: A right triangle has legs of length 6 and 8. What is the length of the hypotenuse?
questions.explanation: By the Pythagorean theorem, the hypotenuse is sqrt(6^2 + 8^2) = sqrt(100) = 10. The value 2 sqrt 7 = sqrt(64 - 36) subtracts the squares instead of adding them.

questions.prompt: In right triangle ABC, angle C is the right angle, AC = 5, BC = 12, and AB = 13. What is the value of sin A?
questions.explanation: The sine of angle A is the side opposite A over the hypotenuse; the side opposite A is BC = 12, so sin A = 12/13. The value 5/13 is cos A, which uses the adjacent side.

questions.prompt: In a right triangle, one acute angle measures x degrees, and sin(x degrees) = 0.6. What is the value of cos((90 - x) degrees)?
questions.explanation: The sine of an acute angle equals the cosine of its complement, so cos((90 - x) degrees) = sin(x degrees) = 0.6. The value 0.8 is cos(x degrees), the cosine of the original angle.

questions.prompt: A right triangle has two acute angles that each measure 45 degrees, and each leg has length 7. What is the length of the hypotenuse?
questions.explanation: In a 45-45-90 triangle, the hypotenuse is sqrt 2 times a leg, so it is 7 sqrt 2. The value 7 sqrt 3 applies to the longer leg of a 30-60-90 triangle, not this triangle.

questions.prompt: In a right triangle, one acute angle measures 30 degrees and the hypotenuse has length 18. What is the length of the side opposite the 30-degree angle?
questions.explanation: In a 30-60-90 triangle, the side opposite the 30-degree angle is half the hypotenuse, so it is 18/2 = 9. The longer leg, opposite the 60-degree angle, would be 9 sqrt 3.

questions.prompt: A 13-foot ladder leans against a vertical wall. The base of the ladder is on level ground 5 feet from the wall. How many feet above the ground does the top of the ladder touch the wall?
questions.explanation: The ladder is the hypotenuse of a right triangle, so the height is sqrt(13^2 - 5^2) = sqrt(144) = 12 feet. Adding the squares instead gives sqrt 194, which would be longer than the ladder itself.

questions.prompt: In a right triangle, the side opposite acute angle θ has length 9 and the side adjacent to angle θ has length 12. What is the value of tan θ?
questions.explanation: The tangent of an angle is opposite over adjacent: 9/12 = 3/4. The value 3/5 is sin θ, since the hypotenuse is 15.

questions.prompt: A right triangle has legs of length 15 and 20. What is the length of the hypotenuse?
questions.explanation: The hypotenuse is sqrt(15^2 + 20^2) = sqrt(225 + 400) = sqrt(625) = 25. This is a 3-4-5 right triangle scaled by 5.

questions.prompt: A circle has a radius of 5 inches. What is the circumference of the circle, in inches?
questions.explanation: The circumference is 2 pi r = 2 pi (5) = 10 pi inches. The value 25 pi is the area, pi r^2.

questions.prompt: A circle has a diameter of 12 meters. What is the area of the circle, in square meters?
questions.explanation: The radius is 12/2 = 6, so the area is pi(6^2) = 36 pi square meters. Using the diameter as the radius gives 144 pi.

questions.prompt: A circle in the xy-plane has equation (x - 2)^2 + (y + 5)^2 = 49. What are the center and radius of the circle?
questions.explanation: The form (x - h)^2 + (y - k)^2 = r^2 has center (h, k) and radius r. Here h = 2, k = -5, and r^2 = 49, so r = 7; reading 49 as the radius forgets that the right side is the square of the radius.

questions.prompt: A circle has a radius of 8. A central angle of the circle measures 90 degrees. The length of the arc intercepted by this angle is kπ. What is the value of k?
questions.explanation: The arc is 90/360 = 1/4 of the circumference, and the circumference is 2 pi(8) = 16 pi, so the arc length is 4 pi and k = 4.

questions.prompt: Line l is tangent to a circle with center O at point P. What is the measure, in degrees, of the angle formed by line l and radius OP?
questions.explanation: A tangent line is perpendicular to the radius drawn to the point of tangency, so the angle is 90 degrees. The tangent does not pass through the center, so the angle cannot be 180 degrees.

questions.prompt: An inscribed angle in a circle intercepts an arc that measures 110 degrees. What is the measure, in degrees, of the inscribed angle?
questions.explanation: An inscribed angle measures half of its intercepted arc, so it measures 110/2 = 55 degrees. The value 110 is the measure of a central angle that intercepts the same arc.

questions.prompt: Which equation represents a circle in the xy-plane with center (0, 0) and radius 6?
questions.explanation: A circle with center (0, 0) and radius r has equation x^2 + y^2 = r^2, so the equation is x^2 + y^2 = 36. The equation x^2 + y^2 = 6 has radius sqrt 6, not 6.

questions.prompt: The length of a rectangle is 3 times its width. The perimeter of the rectangle is 64 centimeters. What is the area of the rectangle, in square centimeters?
questions.explanation: If the width is w, then 2(w + 3w) = 64, so 8w = 64 and w = 8; the length is 24 and the area is 8 x 24 = 192. The value 256 results from treating the rectangle as a square with side 16.

questions.prompt: A right circular cone has a base radius of 6 inches and a height of 8 inches. What is the volume of the cone, in cubic inches?
questions.explanation: The volume of a cone is (1/3) pi r^2 h = (1/3) pi (36)(8) = 96 pi. The value 288 pi is the volume of a cylinder with the same base and height, because it omits the factor of 1/3.

questions.prompt: A square has a diagonal of length 10. What is the area of the square?
questions.explanation: The side of a square with diagonal d is d / sqrt 2, so the side is 10 / sqrt 2 and the area is 100/2 = 50. Squaring the diagonal (100) gives twice the area.

questions.prompt: A rectangular fish tank has inside dimensions of 50 centimeters by 40 centimeters by 30 centimeters. How many liters of water can the tank hold when full? (1 liter = 1,000 cubic centimeters)
questions.explanation: The volume is 50 x 40 x 30 = 60,000 cubic centimeters, and dividing by 1,000 gives 60 liters. Dividing by 100 instead of 1,000 gives 600.

questions.prompt: The length and width of a rectangle are both multiplied by 3. The area of the new rectangle is how many times the area of the original rectangle?
questions.explanation: The new area is (3L)(3W) = 9LW, which is 9 times the original area. Scaling each dimension by 3 does not scale the area by 3; area scales by the square of the factor.

questions.prompt: A right circular cylinder has a volume of 72π cubic units and a radius of 3 units. What is the height of the cylinder, in units?
questions.explanation: Using V = pi r^2 h, 72 pi = pi(9)h, so h = 72/9 = 8. Dividing by 3 instead of 9 forgets to square the radius.

questions.prompt: A figure is made of a rectangle with sides of length 10 and 6 and a semicircle whose diameter is one of the sides of length 6. The semicircle lies outside the rectangle. What is the total area of the figure?
questions.explanation: The semicircle has radius 3, so its area is (1/2) pi (3^2) = 4.5 pi, and the total area is 60 + 4.5 pi. Using the full circle area, 9 pi, ignores that only half of the circle is included.

questions.prompt: The total surface area of a cube is 150 square inches. What is the volume of the cube, in cubic inches?
questions.explanation: A cube has 6 congruent square faces, so each face has area 150/6 = 25 and each edge is 5 inches. The volume is 5^3 = 125; the value 25 is the area of one face.

questions.prompt: An equilateral triangle has a side length of 6. What is the area of the triangle?
questions.explanation: The height of the triangle is 3 sqrt 3, so the area is (1/2)(6)(3 sqrt 3) = 9 sqrt 3. Forgetting the factor of 1/2 gives 18 sqrt 3.

questions.prompt: Parallel lines l and m are cut by a transversal. Two same-side interior angles formed between l and m measure (2x + 15) degrees and (3x - 20) degrees. What is the measure, in degrees, of the larger of these two angles?
questions.explanation: Same-side interior angles are supplementary, so 5x - 5 = 180 and x = 37; the angles measure 89 and 91 degrees, and the larger is 91. Setting the angles equal gives x = 35, which would apply only to congruent angle pairs.

questions.prompt: Each exterior angle of a regular polygon measures 24 degrees. How many sides does the polygon have?
questions.explanation: The exterior angles of any polygon sum to 360 degrees, so a regular polygon with 24-degree exterior angles has 360/24 = 15 sides.

questions.prompt: In triangle ABC, point D lies on side AB and point E lies on side AC so that segment DE is parallel to side BC. If AD = 4, DB = 6, and DE = 5, what is the length of BC?
questions.explanation: Because DE is parallel to BC, triangle ADE is similar to triangle ABC with ratio AD/AB = 4/10. Then BC = 5 x (10/4) = 12.5; using DB instead of AB gives 5 x 6/4 = 7.5, which is a common error.

questions.prompt: The measures of the angles of a triangle are in the ratio 2 : 3 : 7. What is the measure, in degrees, of the largest angle?
questions.explanation: The angles are 2k, 3k, and 7k with 12k = 180, so k = 15 and the largest angle is 7(15) = 105 degrees. The value 75 is the sum of the two smaller angles.

questions.prompt: Two angles are complementary. The measure of the larger angle is 15 degrees less than 4 times the measure of the smaller angle. What is the measure, in degrees, of the larger angle?
questions.explanation: If the smaller angle is s, then s + (4s - 15) = 90, so 5s = 105 and s = 21. The larger angle is 4(21) - 15 = 69 degrees.

questions.prompt: An isosceles triangle has two sides with lengths 4 and 9. What is the perimeter of the triangle?
questions.explanation: The triangle's sides are either 4, 4, 9 or 9, 9, 4. Since 4 + 4 < 9, the first set fails the triangle inequality, so the sides are 9, 9, 4 and the perimeter is 22; the perimeter 17 comes from the impossible triangle.

questions.prompt: What is the measure, in degrees, of each interior angle of a regular octagon?
questions.explanation: The interior angles of an octagon sum to (8 - 2)180 = 1,080 degrees, so each angle of a regular octagon measures 1,080/8 = 135 degrees. The value 45 is the exterior angle.

questions.prompt: In triangle PQR, angle P measures 50 degrees and angle Q measures 70 degrees. The bisector of angle R intersects side PQ at point S. What is the measure, in degrees, of angle PSR?
questions.explanation: Angle R measures 180 - 50 - 70 = 60 degrees, so the bisector makes angle PRS = 30 degrees. In triangle PSR, angle PSR = 180 - 50 - 30 = 100 degrees; the value 80 is angle QSR, the supplement.

questions.prompt: Two similar triangles have corresponding sides in the ratio 2 : 5. The area of the smaller triangle is 12 square units. What is the area, in square units, of the larger triangle?
questions.explanation: The ratio of the areas of similar figures is the square of the ratio of their sides, so the area ratio is 4 : 25. The larger area is 12 x 25/4 = 75; using the side ratio 5/2 gives 30, which is not correct for areas.

questions.prompt: For acute angles with measures x degrees and y degrees, sin(x degrees) = cos(y degrees). If x = 2k + 10 and y = 3k + 5, what is the value of k?
questions.explanation: For acute angles, sin x = cos y exactly when x + y = 90, so 5k + 15 = 90 and k = 15. Setting x equal to y gives k = 5, which confuses complementary angles with equal angles.

questions.prompt: In a right triangle, tan A = 5/12 for acute angle A, and the hypotenuse has length 26. What is the length of the side opposite angle A?
questions.explanation: A tangent of 5/12 matches a 5-12-13 right triangle; scaling by 26/13 = 2 gives legs 10 and 24. The side opposite A corresponds to 5, so its length is 10; the value 24 is the adjacent side.

questions.prompt: In right triangle ABC, angle C is the right angle, and cos B = 0.8. What is the value of sin B?
questions.explanation: Since sin^2 B + cos^2 B = 1, sin B = sqrt(1 - 0.64) = sqrt(0.36) = 0.6, or 3/5. This matches a 3-4-5 right triangle in which the side adjacent to B is 4 and the hypotenuse is 5.

questions.prompt: An isosceles right triangle has a hypotenuse of length 10. What is the area of the triangle?
questions.explanation: Each leg has length 10 / sqrt 2 = 5 sqrt 2, so the area is (1/2)(5 sqrt 2)^2 = (1/2)(50) = 25. The value 50 forgets the factor of 1/2.

questions.prompt: From a point on level ground 40 meters from the base of a vertical tower, the angle of elevation to the top of the tower is 30 degrees. What is the height of the tower, in meters?
questions.explanation: The height is opposite the 30-degree angle and 40 meters is adjacent, so the height is 40 tan 30 degrees = 40 / sqrt 3 = 40 sqrt 3 / 3. The value 40 sqrt 3 uses tan 60 degrees instead of tan 30 degrees.

questions.prompt: In a 30-60-90 triangle, the longer leg has length 9. What is the length of the hypotenuse?
questions.explanation: The longer leg is sqrt 3 times the shorter leg, so the shorter leg is 9 / sqrt 3 = 3 sqrt 3, and the hypotenuse is twice that, 6 sqrt 3. The value 18 doubles the longer leg instead of the shorter leg.

questions.prompt: A rectangle has a width of 9 inches and a diagonal of 15 inches. What is the area of the rectangle, in square inches?
questions.explanation: The diagonal splits the rectangle into right triangles, so the length is sqrt(15^2 - 9^2) = sqrt 144 = 12. The area is 9 x 12 = 108 square inches.

questions.prompt: What is the measure of a 150-degree angle in radians?
questions.explanation: To convert degrees to radians, multiply by pi/180: 150(pi/180) = 5 pi/6. The value 5 pi/3 corresponds to 300 degrees.

questions.prompt: A circle in the xy-plane has equation x^2 + y^2 - 6x + 4y = 12. What is the radius of the circle?
questions.explanation: Completing the square gives (x - 3)^2 + (y + 2)^2 = 12 + 9 + 4 = 25, so the radius is sqrt 25 = 5. The value sqrt 12 ignores the constants added while completing the square.

questions.prompt: A circle has a radius of 6. A sector of the circle has a central angle of 120 degrees. The area of the sector is kπ. What is the value of k?
questions.explanation: The sector is 120/360 = 1/3 of the circle, and the circle's area is 36 pi, so the sector's area is 12 pi and k = 12.

questions.prompt: A circle in the xy-plane has equation (x - 1)^2 + (y + 2)^2 = 25. Which of the following points lies on the circle?
questions.explanation: Substituting (4, 2) gives (4 - 1)^2 + (2 + 2)^2 = 9 + 16 = 25, so it is on the circle. The point (4, -2) is only 3 units from the center (1, -2), so it lies inside the circle.

questions.prompt: Triangle ABC is inscribed in a circle, and side AB is a diameter of the circle. If AB = 10 and AC = 6, what is the length of BC?
questions.explanation: An angle inscribed in a semicircle is a right angle, so angle C is 90 degrees and BC = sqrt(10^2 - 6^2) = 8. The value 2 sqrt 34 = sqrt(100 + 36) wrongly treats AB as a leg.

questions.prompt: A circle has a circumference of 36π. An arc of the circle has length 6π. What is the measure, in degrees, of the central angle that intercepts this arc?
questions.explanation: The arc is 6 pi / 36 pi = 1/6 of the circumference, so the central angle is 360/6 = 60 degrees. The value 30 would be the measure of an inscribed angle intercepting the arc.

questions.prompt: From point P outside a circle, segments PA and PB are drawn tangent to the circle at points A and B. If PA = 3x + 2 and PB = 5x - 8, what is the length of PA?
questions.explanation: Tangent segments from the same external point are congruent, so 3x + 2 = 5x - 8, which gives x = 5 and PA = 3(5) + 2 = 17. The value 5 is x, not the length of PA.

questions.prompt: A circle has a radius of 4 centimeters. A central angle of the circle measures 2.5 radians. What is the length, in centimeters, of the arc intercepted by this angle?
questions.explanation: For an angle in radians, arc length equals radius times angle: s = 4 x 2.5 = 10 centimeters. Using the degree formula with 2.5 treated as degrees would give a much smaller arc.

questions.prompt: A circle in the xy-plane has center (-3, 1) and passes through the point (1, 4). Which equation represents the circle?
questions.explanation: The radius is the distance from (-3, 1) to (1, 4): sqrt(4^2 + 3^2) = 5, so r^2 = 25 and the equation is (x + 3)^2 + (y - 1)^2 = 25. Writing 5 on the right side uses the radius instead of its square.

questions.prompt: The radius of a right circular cylinder is increased by 20%, and its height is decreased by 20%. How does the volume of the new cylinder compare with the volume of the original cylinder?
questions.explanation: The volume is proportional to r^2 h, so the new volume is (1.2)^2(0.8) = 1.44(0.8) = 1.152 times the original, an increase of 15.2%. Assuming the changes cancel ignores that the radius is squared; 4% less is the result of (1.2)(0.8) without squaring.

questions.prompt: The radius of a right circular cone is twice the radius of a right circular cylinder, and the height of the cylinder is 3 times the height of the cone. The volume of the cone is what fraction of the volume of the cylinder?
questions.explanation: If the cylinder has radius r and the cone has height h, the cone's volume is (1/3) pi (2r)^2 h = (4/3) pi r^2 h and the cylinder's volume is pi r^2 (3h) = 3 pi r^2 h. The ratio is (4/3)/3 = 4/9.

questions.prompt: A square is inscribed in a circle of radius 6, so that all four vertices of the square lie on the circle. What is the area of the region inside the circle but outside the square?
questions.explanation: The diagonal of the square is a diameter, 12, so the square's area is 12^2/2 = 72, and the region's area is 36 pi - 72. The expression 144 - 36 pi uses a square whose side is 12, which would circumscribe the circle instead.

questions.prompt: A sphere is inscribed in a cube with edge length 10 centimeters, so that the sphere touches each face of the cube. What is the volume, in cubic centimeters, of the space inside the cube but outside the sphere?
questions.explanation: The sphere's diameter equals the edge length, so its radius is 5 and its volume is (4/3) pi (125) = (500/3) pi. Subtracting from 1,000 gives the answer; using a radius of 10 gives (4,000/3) pi, which is larger than the cube itself.

questions.prompt: A rectangle has a perimeter of 50 and a diagonal of length √325. What is the area of the rectangle?
questions.explanation: If the sides are l and w, then l + w = 25 and l^2 + w^2 = 325. Since (l + w)^2 = l^2 + w^2 + 2lw, we get 625 = 325 + 2lw, so lw = 150 (the sides are 10 and 15).

questions.prompt: A right circular cylinder with a radius of 8 centimeters is partially filled with water. A solid metal sphere with a radius of 6 centimeters is placed in the cylinder and is completely submerged. By how many centimeters does the water level rise?
questions.explanation: The water rises by the sphere's volume divided by the cylinder's base area: (4/3) pi (216) / (64 pi) = 288/64 = 4.5 centimeters. Dividing the radii or ignoring the 4/3 factor leads to the other values.

questions.prompt: A regular hexagon has a side length of 4. What is the area of the hexagon?
questions.explanation: A regular hexagon can be divided into 6 equilateral triangles with side 4, each with area (sqrt 3/4)(16) = 4 sqrt 3. The total area is 6(4 sqrt 3) = 24 sqrt 3; using only 4 triangles gives 16 sqrt 3.

questions.prompt: In the xy-plane, a triangle has vertices at (1, 2), (7, 5), and (4, 9). What is the area of the triangle?
questions.explanation: Enclose the triangle in the rectangle from x = 1 to 7 and y = 2 to 9, which has area 42, and subtract the three outer right triangles with areas 9, 6, and 10.5, leaving 16.5. The value 33 is twice the area, which results from forgetting to divide by 2 in the coordinate formula.

questions.prompt: A right rectangular prism has a square base and a height of 5 inches. The volume of the prism is 245 cubic inches. What is the total surface area of the prism, in square inches?
questions.explanation: The base area is 245/5 = 49, so each base edge is 7. The surface area is 2(49) + 4(7 x 5) = 98 + 140 = 238 square inches.

questions.prompt: Two circles have the same center. A chord of the larger circle is tangent to the smaller circle, and the length of this chord is 16. What is the area of the region between the two circles?
questions.explanation: The radius of the smaller circle meets the chord at its midpoint at a right angle, so R^2 = r^2 + 8^2 and R^2 - r^2 = 64. The area between the circles is pi R^2 - pi r^2 = 64 pi; the value 256 pi uses the full chord instead of half of it.

questions.prompt: In right triangle ABC, angle C is the right angle. The altitude from C to hypotenuse AB meets AB at point D, so that AD = 4 and DB = 9. What is the length of CD?
questions.explanation: The altitude to the hypotenuse creates two triangles similar to each other, so AD/CD = CD/DB and CD^2 = 4 x 9 = 36. Therefore CD = 6; the value 6.5 is the average of 4 and 9, not their geometric mean.

questions.prompt: In triangle ABC, point D lies on side AB and point E lies on side AC so that segment DE is parallel to side BC, and AD : DB = 2 : 3. The area of triangle ADE is 12. What is the area of the region inside triangle ABC but outside triangle ADE?
questions.explanation: Triangle ADE is similar to triangle ABC with ratio AD : AB = 2 : 5, so the area ratio is 4 : 25 and the area of ABC is 12(25/4) = 75. The remaining region has area 75 - 12 = 63; using the ratio 2 : 3 instead of 2 : 5 gives 27.

questions.prompt: The angles of a triangle measure (x + 20) degrees, (2x - 10) degrees, and (3x - 40) degrees. What is the measure, in degrees, of an exterior angle at the vertex with the smallest interior angle?
questions.explanation: The angles sum to 6x - 30 = 180, so x = 35 and the angles are 55, 60, and 65 degrees. The exterior angle at the 55-degree vertex is 180 - 55 = 125 degrees; 55 is the interior angle itself.

questions.prompt: Each interior angle of a regular polygon is 7 times as large as each of its exterior angles. How many sides does the polygon have?
questions.explanation: An interior angle and its exterior angle sum to 180 degrees, so 8e = 180 and each exterior angle is 22.5 degrees. The number of sides is 360/22.5 = 16.

questions.prompt: In triangle ABC, point D lies on side AC so that angle ABD is congruent to angle ACB. If AB = 6 and AC = 9, what is the length of AD?
questions.explanation: Triangles ABD and ACB share angle A and have angle ABD congruent to angle ACB, so they are similar with AB/AC = AD/AB. Then AD = AB^2/AC = 36/9 = 4; the value 13.5 comes from setting up the proportion upside down.

questions.prompt: A triangle has sides of length 7, 11, and x, where x is an integer. How many different values of x are possible?
questions.explanation: By the triangle inequality, 11 - 7 < x < 11 + 7, so 4 < x < 18 and x can be any integer from 5 to 17, which is 17 - 5 + 1 = 13 values. Answering 12 comes from subtracting the endpoints (17 - 5) without adding 1, and 14 incorrectly includes one of the excluded endpoints.

questions.prompt: Parallel lines l and m are cut by a transversal t. One angle formed by t and l measures (5x - 12) degrees, and the corresponding angle formed by t and m measures (3x + 20) degrees. What is the measure, in degrees, of an angle that forms a linear pair with the angle measuring (5x - 12) degrees?
questions.explanation: Corresponding angles formed by parallel lines are congruent, so 5x - 12 = 3x + 20 and x = 16, making the angle 68 degrees. An angle forming a linear pair with it measures 180 - 68 = 112 degrees.

questions.prompt: In isosceles triangle ABC, AB = AC and angle A measures 36 degrees. The bisector of angle B intersects side AC at point D. What is the measure, in degrees, of angle BDC?
questions.explanation: The base angles are (180 - 36)/2 = 72 degrees, so angle ABD = 36 degrees. Angle BDC is an exterior angle of triangle ABD, so it equals 36 + 36 = 72 degrees; the value 108 is angle ADB.

questions.prompt: For acute angle θ, sin θ = 5/13. What is the value of tan(90 degrees - θ)?
questions.explanation: With sin θ = 5/13, the sides are 5, 12, 13, so tan θ = 5/12. The tangent of the complement is the reciprocal, 12/5; choosing 5/12 gives tan θ itself.

questions.prompt: An angle measures 5π/12 radians. What is the measure of this angle in degrees?
questions.explanation: Multiply by 180/pi to convert radians to degrees: (5 pi/12)(180/pi) = 5(15) = 75 degrees.

questions.prompt: In right triangle ABC, angle C is the right angle, cos A = 0.6, and AB = 20. What is the length of the altitude from C to side AB?
questions.explanation: AC = 20(0.6) = 12 and BC = 16, so the area is (1/2)(12)(16) = 96. Setting (1/2)(20)h = 96 gives h = 9.6; the values 12 and 16 are the legs, not the altitude to the hypotenuse.

questions.prompt: For acute angle x, cos x = 2/3. What is the value of (sin x)(tan x)?
questions.explanation: sin x = sqrt(1 - 4/9) = sqrt 5/3 and tan x = (sqrt 5/3)/(2/3) = sqrt 5/2. Their product is 5/6; the value 5/9 is sin^2 x.

questions.prompt: What is the value of cos(7π/6)?
questions.explanation: The angle 7 pi/6 is 210 degrees, in the third quadrant where cosine is negative, with reference angle 30 degrees. So cos(7 pi/6) = -cos 30 degrees = -sqrt 3/2; the value -1/2 is sin(7 pi/6).

questions.prompt: In triangle ABC, angle B is a right angle, angle A measures 30 degrees, and AC = 16. Point D lies on AC so that BD is perpendicular to AC. What is the length of AD?
questions.explanation: AB = 16 cos 30 degrees = 8 sqrt 3. In right triangle ABD, AD = AB cos 30 degrees = 8 sqrt 3 (sqrt 3/2) = 12.

questions.prompt: An isosceles triangle has two sides of length 10 and a base of length 12. What is the sine of one of the base angles?
questions.explanation: The altitude to the base bisects it, forming right triangles with legs 6 and 8 and hypotenuse 10. The sine of a base angle is opposite over hypotenuse, 8/10 = 4/5; the value 3/5 is the cosine.

questions.prompt: From point A on level ground, the angle of elevation to the top of a building is 45 degrees. From point B, which is 30 meters closer to the building along the same straight line, the angle of elevation is 60 degrees. What is the height of the building, in meters?
questions.explanation: If the height is h, the distances from the building are h/tan 45 degrees = h and h/tan 60 degrees = h/sqrt 3, so h - h/sqrt 3 = 30. Solving gives h = 30 sqrt 3/(sqrt 3 - 1) = 45 + 15 sqrt 3, about 71 meters.

questions.prompt: The equation x^2 + y^2 + 8x - 10y + c = 0 represents a circle with radius 7 in the xy-plane. What is the value of c?
questions.explanation: Completing the square gives (x + 4)^2 + (y - 5)^2 = 16 + 25 - c, so 41 - c = 49 and c = -8. Choosing 8 comes from a sign error when moving c to the other side.

questions.prompt: A circle in the xy-plane has equation 2x^2 + 2y^2 - 12x + 8y - 46 = 0. What is the radius of the circle?
questions.explanation: Divide by 2 to get x^2 + y^2 - 6x + 4y = 23, then complete the square: (x - 3)^2 + (y + 2)^2 = 23 + 9 + 4 = 36. The radius is 6; forgetting to divide by 2 first gives an incorrect radius.

questions.prompt: Points A and B lie on a circle with center O and radius 12. The length of minor arc AB is 10π. What is the measure of angle AOB, in radians?
questions.explanation: For an angle in radians, arc length = radius x angle, so the angle is 10 pi / 12 = 5 pi/6 radians. The value 5 pi/12 would follow from using the diameter, 24, in place of the radius.

questions.prompt: A chord of a circle has length 24, and the distance from the center of the circle to the chord is 5. What is the area of the circle?
questions.explanation: The perpendicular from the center bisects the chord, forming a right triangle with legs 12 and 5, so the radius is 13. The area is 169 pi; using 12 as the radius gives 144 pi.

questions.prompt: Points A, B, and C lie on a circle with center O, and C is not on minor arc AB. Inscribed angle ACB measures π/5 radians. The central angle AOB measures kπ radians. What is the value of k?
questions.explanation: A central angle is twice an inscribed angle that intercepts the same arc, so angle AOB = 2(pi/5) = 2 pi/5 radians. Therefore k = 2/5.

questions.prompt: A circle in the xy-plane is tangent to both the x-axis and the y-axis, has its center in the first quadrant, and passes through the point (2, 1). What is the sum of all possible values of the radius of the circle?
questions.explanation: A circle tangent to both axes with center in the first quadrant has center (r, r), so (2 - r)^2 + (1 - r)^2 = r^2, which simplifies to r^2 - 6r + 5 = 0. The radii are 1 and 5, whose sum is 6; choosing 5 gives only the larger radius.

questions.prompt: The line y = x + 1 intersects the circle x^2 + y^2 = 13 at two points. What is the distance between these two points?
questions.explanation: Substituting gives x^2 + (x + 1)^2 = 13, so x^2 + x - 6 = 0 and x = 2 or x = -3; the points are (2, 3) and (-3, -2). The distance is sqrt(5^2 + 5^2) = 5 sqrt 2; the value 5 is only the horizontal distance.

questions.passage: The axolotl, a salamander native to lakes near Mexico City, can regrow lost limbs, parts of its spinal cord, and even portions of its heart. Unlike humans, whose wounds typically close with scar tissue, axolotls form a cluster of cells at the injury site that rebuilds the missing structure. Biologists study these animals closely, hoping that understanding their regenerative abilities might someday help improve medical treatments for people.
questions.prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Human wounds heal more slowly than axolotl wounds because human cells are less active.
Biologists have already used axolotl research to develop new treatments for heart disease.
The axolotl's unusual ability to regrow body parts makes it a valuable subject for scientists interested in medicine.
Axolotls are found only in lakes near Mexico City and nowhere else in the world.
questions.explanation: The text describes the axolotl's regenerative abilities and explains that biologists study them hoping to improve medical treatments, which matches the correct choice. The option about new heart-disease treatments goes too far: the text says scientists hope this may happen 'someday,' not that it already has.

questions.passage:

Every spring, Nana Ruth knelt in the same corner of the yard and pressed seeds into the soil with her thumb, one at a time. She never used a measuring stick or a garden plan. When I asked how she knew where each seed belonged, she laughed and tapped her temple. "Forty years of tomatoes," she said. "The ground and I have an understanding."
questions.prompt: Based on the text, how does Nana Ruth approach gardening?
options: She relies on long experience rather than formal tools or plans.
She carefully measures the distance between seeds each year.
She plants her garden in a different spot every spring.
She asks the narrator for advice about where to plant seeds.
questions.explanation: Nana Ruth uses no measuring stick or plan and credits 'forty years of tomatoes' for her knowledge, showing she relies on experience. The option about measuring contradicts the text, which says she never used a measuring stick.

questions.passage: Between 1883 and 1929, the industrialist Andrew Carnegie funded the construction of more than 2,500 public libraries, most of them in the United States. Towns that received money had to agree to provide land for the building and to pay for the library's upkeep with public funds. This requirement meant that communities, not just Carnegie, were responsible for keeping the libraries open over time.
questions.prompt: According to the text, what did towns have to do in order to receive Carnegie's library funding?
options: Agree to name the library after Andrew Carnegie
Build the library before Carnegie would send any money
Provide land and commit public money to maintain the library
Raise enough private donations to match Carnegie's gift
questions.explanation: The text states that towns had to provide land and pay for upkeep with public funds. Matching private donations is never mentioned; the text emphasizes public, not private, funding.

questions.passage: Cities are often several degrees warmer than the countryside around them, a pattern known as the urban heat island effect. Dark surfaces such as asphalt roads and rooftops absorb sunlight during the day and release that heat slowly at night. In addition, cities usually have fewer trees, which cool their surroundings by providing shade and releasing water vapor. Planting trees and using lighter-colored roofing are two ways cities are trying to reduce the effect.
questions.prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Asphalt roads are the single most important cause of rising temperatures around the world.
Planting trees in cities has completely solved the problem of urban heat islands.
Cities tend to be warmer than nearby rural areas because of their surfaces and lack of trees, but steps can be taken to reduce this difference.
Rural areas are cooler than cities mainly because they receive less sunlight each day.
questions.explanation: The text explains the urban heat island effect, its causes (dark surfaces, few trees), and possible remedies. The option claiming the problem has been 'completely solved' overstates the text, which says cities are only 'trying to reduce' the effect.

questions.passage: Kintsugi is a Japanese technique for repairing broken pottery with lacquer mixed with powdered gold. Instead of hiding the cracks, the repair makes them shine. Many people connect the practice to the idea that damage and repair are part of an object's history and need not be concealed. A bowl mended this way is often valued more highly than it was before it broke.
questions.prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Kintsugi repairs pottery in a way that highlights, rather than hides, its damage, reflecting a view that repair is part of an object's story.
Kintsugi was invented to make cheap pottery look more expensive.
Kintsugi is the most common way of repairing pottery in Japan today.
Pottery repaired with gold is stronger than pottery that has never been broken.
questions.explanation: The text focuses on how kintsugi makes cracks visible and on the idea that damage is part of an object's history. The claim about strength is never made; the text discusses value, not durability.

questions.passage:

Marisol stood in the wings, gripping her violin so tightly that her knuckles whitened. Through the curtain she could hear the audience shifting in their seats, a sound like distant waves. She closed her eyes and played the opening bars of the sonata in her mind, as she had a thousand times in her bedroom. Slowly, her fingers loosened.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes what happens in the text?
options: A violinist decides not to perform because the audience is too noisy.
A performer is distracted from her music by the sound of the ocean.
A musician practices in her bedroom before a concert begins.
A nervous performer calms herself by mentally rehearsing her music.
questions.explanation: Marisol is tense at first, then mentally plays the sonata and her fingers loosen, showing she calms herself. The bedroom option misreads the text: her bedroom practice is something she remembers, not what happens in the scene.

questions.passage: In one well-known set of experiments, researchers asked participants to assemble simple storage boxes and then asked how much they would pay for them. Participants offered noticeably more for boxes they had built themselves than for identical, pre-assembled boxes. The researchers called this tendency the "IKEA effect": people place extra value on things they have helped create, even when the result is no better than what others have made.
questions.prompt: According to the text, what did the experiments show?
options: Boxes built by participants were better made than pre-assembled boxes.
People were unwilling to pay for any boxes that they had not built themselves.
Participants preferred buying pre-assembled boxes because they saved time.
People valued boxes they had assembled more highly than identical boxes they had not assembled.
questions.explanation: The text says participants offered more for boxes they built than for identical pre-assembled ones. The text explicitly says the self-built result is 'no better' than others' work, so the quality option is wrong.

questions.passage: Tardigrades are tiny animals, usually less than a millimeter long, that live in moss, soil, and water. When their surroundings dry out, many tardigrades pull in their legs, lose most of the water in their bodies, and enter a state called a tun. In this condition they can survive for years. When water returns, they rehydrate and resume normal activity within hours.
questions.prompt: According to the text, what do many tardigrades do when their environment dries out?
options: They lose most of their body water and enter a dormant state called a tun.
They die within hours unless water returns quickly.
They grow larger so they can store extra water in their bodies.
They move to a wetter environment such as a lake or pond.
questions.explanation: The text states that tardigrades lose most of their water and enter a tun, in which they can survive for years. The option about dying within hours confuses the detail that they resume activity within hours after water returns.

questions.passage: For decades, historians described medieval European peasants as almost entirely cut off from the wider world, rarely traveling beyond their villages. Recent analysis of court records, pilgrimage accounts, and market tolls has complicated that picture. These documents show peasants walking to regional fairs, traveling to distant shrines, and appearing as witnesses in courts many miles from home. While most peasants did spend much of their lives near their birthplace, their world was evidently less closed than once assumed.
questions.prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: New evidence suggests that medieval peasants traveled and interacted beyond their villages more than historians once believed.
Historians have long overestimated how often medieval peasants traveled.
Court records are the most reliable source of information about medieval peasants.
Most medieval peasants regularly made long journeys to distant shrines and courts.
questions.explanation: The text contrasts an older view of isolated peasants with newer evidence of travel and concludes their world was 'less closed than once assumed.' The option claiming most peasants 'regularly' made long journeys overstates the text, which notes that most stayed near their birthplace.

questions.passage: Honeybee colonies regulate the temperature of their brood, the developing young, with surprising precision, keeping it between about 32 and 36 degrees Celsius. On cold days, worker bees cluster over the brood and shiver their flight muscles to produce heat. On hot days, they fan their wings to circulate air and spread droplets of water that cool the hive as they evaporate. Because brood raised outside this range can develop abnormalities, this temperature control is vital to the colony's survival.
questions.prompt: According to the text, why is temperature regulation important to a honeybee colony?
options: The honey stored in the hive spoils if temperatures rise too high.
Worker bees cannot fly unless the hive remains between 32 and 36 degrees Celsius.
Young bees that develop at temperatures outside a narrow range may grow abnormally.
Shivering and fanning help worker bees build stronger flight muscles.
questions.explanation: The final sentence explains that brood raised outside the range 'can develop abnormalities,' which is why control is vital. The flight option misapplies the temperature range, which the text connects to the brood, not to adult flight.

questions.passage:
